description: The plot illustrates training loss over time for two methods, comparing a “Vanilla” run to “SepLLM.” The x-axis is labeled “Training Time (s)” on a linear scale, spanning from 0 to 250,000 seconds with regularly spaced tick labels every 50,000 seconds. The y-axis is labeled “Loss” on a linear scale, ranging from 2.40 to 2.75 with tick labels at 0.05 intervals. The Vanilla series is shown as a purple solid line with triangle markers; it starts near the top of the axis around 2.75 at early times, then decreases smoothly, reaching about 2.62 near 50,000 s, about 2.57 near 100,000 s, about 2.54 near 150,000 s, and approaching roughly 2.50 by 250,000 s. The SepLLM series is shown as a red solid line with circular markers; it begins around 2.71 at early times, declines steadily to about 2.61 near 50,000 s, about 2.56 near 100,000 s, about 2.52 near 150,000 s, and ends just under 2.50 (around 2.49) by roughly 230,000–240,000 s. A green dashed horizontal reference line is drawn at loss = 2.50, and green dashed vertical guides with a double-headed arrow annotate a “1.26×” span between approximately 200,000 s and 250,000 s at the 2.50 loss level.
